name: Ancient Stone Guardian
shortDesc: Tall, mindless construct tasked with the protection of places or objects.
body:
Carved from bedrock and bound by forgotten rites of warding, stone guardians stand vigil over ancient sanctums, deep vaults, and forgotten tombs. Cloaked in centuries of dust and creeping moss, they rest in deceptive stillness, appearing indistinguishable from ordinary weathered statuary to the unwary traveler. Yet beneath that calcified exterior lies an unblinking, tireless purpose waiting for the singular transgression that breaches their sacred perimeter.

The moment their ward is disturbed, long-dormant runes flare to life along their granite limbs with a bone-jarring groan of grinding rock. Once roused, a guardian knows neither fatigue, doubt, nor mercy. Driven by the unyielding logic of its ancient mandate, it cannot return to its stony slumber until the trespasser has been thoroughly eradicated—a terrifying, inexorable testament to the enduring craft of its creators.
behaviors: Ignores parley, pain, and tactical feints.
Prioritizes crushing the nearest active threat.
scholarQuote: "Flesh grows weary, and the mortal heart can be reasoned with, frightened, or broken. But an oath carved into bedrock possesses neither pity nor doubt; once stirred, it is unstoppable."

name: Crawling Grave
body:
Usually born from atrocities too terrible for the earth to swallow, crawling graves stir within unhallowed trenches, plague pits, and the forgotten ditches of wartime slaughter. Where countless lives are violently snuffed out and discarded without rites or mourning, the concentrated residue of their terror curdles the surrounding soil. In time, this lingering agony binds fractured marrow, shattered ribs, and mismatched skulls into a single skittering horror—a hideous amalgamation of the murdered, coalesced into a unified monument of hatred.

Driven by an insatiable compulsion to expand its necrotic chorus, the heap drags itself forward on hundreds of frantic, clawing fingers. It knows no mortal frailties—needing neither air, nourishment, nor reprieve—only the cold imperative to assimilate the living. As it rolls over its prey, it snaps and weaves their fresh remains into its churning bulk, dragging new victims into its eternal, restless torment.
behaviors: Consumes fresh corpses to absorb bones.
Scuttles relentlessly over obstacles and walls.
Targets wounded prey to expand itself.
scholarQuote: This thing was born from a mass grave? Makes you wonder who the real monster is, doesn't it?

name: Ulnorya
shortDesc: Eight long, writhing tentacles support and propel this snarling horror's oblong body while its jagged maw reveals rows of razor teeth.
scholarQuote: Where the Ulnorya comes from is a mystery. Many think it is a result of the Void corruption that affected the world after the War, but ancient texts mention creatures eerily similar. We shouldn't forget the horrors that roamed the world eons ago.

name: Tainted Velociraptor
shortDesc: Little is known of these creatures. While it is known that some dinosaurs still roam the land, the existence of *tainted* ones remains purely theoretical. If it were to exist, it is safe to say that there little chance for someone to survive this encounter...
body: Its sinewy frame coils with unnatural tension, every muscle taut beneath its mottled plumage of inky black and deep indigo. Vicious talons scrape the ground with each step, and its feathers — once sleek — now jut out in ragged, uneven clumps, as though scorched by shadow. Streaks of seething violet energy pulse beneath its skin, crawling along its limbs and up its neck like veins filled with corrupted ethyria. Its eyes gleam a sickly yellow, alive with a malicious intelligence, burning with a hungry, unnatural gleam — not the mindless hunger of beasts, but something colder, calculated, and wrong. The air warps faintly around its form, and a low, almost imperceptible hum of magic seems to follow its movements — as if the creature exists partially out of phase with the world.

name: Flesh Hound
shortDesc: A shapeless abominable heap of ever shaking muscle, with sharp bones protruding from its face and numerous dark beady eyes.
body: Amongst the many horrors of the Dystopian Weald, Flesh Hounds hold a special place. They are driven by what seems to be an appetite for destruction. Those who made their way up to the Oneiric Fields are found hunting endemic creatures and destroying plant-life. Their presence on other layers of the Dreamlands is a real threat to the balance of the realm.
behaviors: Will attack creatures larger than it
